rationale: Across the literature delineating Ramond-Elliott neurodevelopmental syndrome (RAMELN; OMIM #621421), all 12 reported individuals in the discovery cohort (Ramond et al., 2023) presented with developmental delay and intellectual disability (12/12, 100%), and the subsequent independent case report (Shatokhina et al., 2023) brought the cumulative count to 13/13 (100%). In contrast, seizures and infantile spasms were documented as a frequent but incomplete feature, described clinically as occurring in 'about half' of patients (consistent with a penetrance between 50% and 75%). No molecularly confirmed TRA2B patients lacking developmental delay/intellectual disability have been identified.

evidence.text: The discovery study recruited 12 individuals from 11 unrelated families with monoallelic TRA2B variants; all 12 presented with intellectual disability and/or developmental delay (100%), with infantile spasms and epilepsy frequently associated but not universal.

source.title: Clustered variants in the 5' coding region of TRA2B cause a distinctive neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: All affected individuals presented intellectual disability and/or developmental delay, frequently associated with infantile spasms, microcephaly, brain anomalies, autism spectrum disorder, feeding difficulties, and short stature.

evidence.text: The clinical synopsis for OMIM #621421 establishes that seizures occur in about half of individuals affected by Ramond-Elliott neurodevelopmental syndrome.

source.title: Clinical Synopsis - #621421 - RAMOND-ELLIOTT NEURODEVELOPMENTAL SYNDROME; RAMELN

evidence.text: A second case study identified an additional patient carrying a splice variant in TRA2B presenting with seizures and neurodevelopmental delay, extending total molecularly confirmed cases.

source.title: RAMOND-ELLIOTT NEURODEVELOPMENTAL SYNDROME; RAMELN
source.quote: TRA2B gene splice variant linked to seizures and neurodevelopmental delay: a second case study. Int. J. Molec. Sci. 24: 15572, 2023.

new_directions.question_text: Do non-truncating missense variants outside the 5' region of TRA2B cause an attenuated phenotype devoid of infantile spasms or intellectual disability?
new_directions.rationale: All currently identified pathogenic variants cluster in the 5' coding region upstream of the alternative translation start site; screening broader cohorts will clarify if penetrance remains invariant across distinct mutational mechanisms.
